body:
## Desired result

A route with optional captures and a parameter matcher must choose the same page or endpoint as Kit’s client for both matching and nonmatching URLs.

## Acceptance

Demonstrate an omitted optional parameter, a valid matched value, and a rejected value through a Go load or endpoint in development and a built server.

## Current boundary

The matrix says optional captures are decoded, while JavaScript matcher functions are not run by Go.

Feature matrix: https://tylergannon.github.io/skgo/features.html. Kit’s pinned source and client behavior define compatibility.


<!-- agent-session-group-20261018 -->
## Coordinated agent session: Route semantics and matcher qualification

Work together: #163, #159.

Real page/endpoint routes honor supported route options and optional/matched parameters, including canonical redirects, omitted captures and matcher rejection, in development and production. Reuse one representative routing application to qualify the combined route-selection contract. Matcher implementation already exists; #159 is residual qualification/documentation, not a second matcher implementation. Unsupported options need the clear refusal required by #163.

Use the installed pinned Kit implementation as the specification. The session is complete only when both issues' retained acceptance criteria are satisfied; partial delivery does not close the other issue.

comments.body:
This issue may be partly out of date. At v0.36.0 (`3b382953`), Go routing runs parameter matchers through paired Go functions:

- Go matchers are declared next to Kit's `params.ts`: [example/web/src/params.go](https://github.com/tylergannon/skgo/blob/3b382953fb97f77aecd1f5122d76dfbe586fec89/example/web/src/params.go) (`func Order(value string) (OrderNumber, bool)`). Generated code adapts them to `ParamMatcher` ([request_event.go:32-34](https://github.com/tylergannon/skgo/blob/3b382953fb97f77aecd1f5122d76dfbe586fec89/request_event.go#L32-L34)), and `LoadConfig.Matchers`, `EndpointConfig.Matchers` and `HandleConfig.Matchers` consume them. `gen.Config.RouteMetadata` validates the Go declarations against Kit's frontend-validated matcher names ([internal/gen/gen.go:48-50](https://github.com/tylergannon/skgo/blob/3b382953fb97f77aecd1f5122d76dfbe586fec89/internal/gen/gen.go#L48-L50)).
- Optional captures that go through a matcher: [routing_contract_test.go:14-27](https://github.com/tylergannon/skgo/blob/3b382953fb97f77aecd1f5122d76dfbe586fec89/routing_contract_test.go#L14-L27) covers `/[[lang=Lang]]/[[id]]` and `/[[lang=Lang]]/[...rest]`. The matcher is called and rejects, and the load, remote caller and hook all see the same values.
- Browser: "A named Go matcher result reaches a load after Kit navigation" ([example/e2e/features/loads.feature:13-21](https://github.com/tylergannon/skgo/blob/3b382953fb97f77aecd1f5122d76dfbe586fec89/example/e2e/features/loads.feature#L13-L21)) and the `typed-dependencies/[a=Order]/[b=Order]` scenario at loads.feature:45.

Still open against the acceptance text: no browser scenario shows an omitted optional parameter or a rejected matcher value through a Go load or endpoint. The README row ([README.md:228](https://github.com/tylergannon/skgo/blob/3b382953fb97f77aecd1f5122d76dfbe586fec89/README.md#L228)) still says "JavaScript parameter matcher functions are not run by Go". That is literally true, because Go runs its paired matcher, but it reads as if matchers were unsupported. I am leaving the issue open for the maintainer to decide.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

**Triage — 2026-10-18**

Checked against current [`main` at `920b6aca`](https://github.com/tylergannon/skgo/tree/920b6aca738a65d6c046a67f4db2373596fafd03). Classification: `bounded-hard`. 

The missing-matcher implementation claim is stale: paired Go matchers, optional-capture routing and generated matcher validation are present. TestSharedRoutingContracts and TestTypedLoadMatcherRouting passed on current main in this triage. Keep open narrowly for the remaining acceptance: demonstrate omitted optional parameters, valid and rejected matcher values in the real application across development and production, plus clarify the misleading README matcher wording. Do not implement a JavaScript matcher engine in Go.
